title: "Curating the data, part 1: Finn the Wolfhound"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(here)
library(gutenbergr)
library(tidyr)
library(tidytext)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
if (!dir.exists(here("data"))) {
  dir.create(here("data"))
}

if (!file.exists(here("data/finn.rda"))) {
     finn <- gutenberg_download(30550)
     save(finn, file=here("data/finn.rda"))
} else {
     load(here("data/finn.rda"))
}
```

### curating data to remove the outlier words
```{r}
finn_curated <- finn |>
  # 1. Add a line number to keep track of the text order
  mutate(linenumber = row_number()) |>
  
  # 2. Use your manual cut-off to drop the Gutenberg footer at the end of the book
  filter(linenumber < 15000) |> 
  
  # 3. Detect chapters. Every time a line starts with "CHAPTER", it adds 1 to the chapter count.
  mutate(chapter = cumsum(str_detect(text, regex("^CHAPTER", ignore_case = FALSE)))) |>
  
  # 4. Filter out everything BEFORE Chapter 1 (This removes the TOC, Title page, and Intro)
  filter(chapter > 0)

# Take a peek to make sure the first row is now the start of Chapter 1
head(finn_curated)
```



```{r}
finn_curated |> 
  unnest_tokens(output=word, input = text, token = "words") ->
   fw_tokens

head(fw_tokens)
tail(fw_tokens)
```
### Checking the unique words
```{r}
unique(fw_tokens$word) |> length()

```

### We can also check for the most common words
```{r}
fw_tokens |> count(word, sort = TRUE) |> head(20)
```
### since the most commons word might mess with our sentiment data, the stop words need to be replaced. 
```{r}
fw_tokens |> anti_join(stop_words) -> fw_tokens2

unique(fw_tokens2$word) |> length()
nrow(fw_tokens2)
head(fw_tokens2)
```
```{r}
fw_tokens2 |> count(word, sort = TRUE)
```
### We will start exploring the new interesting words that are not common in the english language.
```{r}
fw_tokens2 |> count(word, sort = TRUE) |>
  filter(n > 100) |>
  mutate(word = reorder(word, n)) |>
  
  ggplot(aes(x = word, y = n)) +
  coord_flip() +
  geom_col() +
  labs(y = NULL)
```
### I can see that the msot common words are finn and master, which shows me a good undertanding about the sory and the environment.
